card.summary: Product catalog demo page backed by PGDataLayer
card.description: Create a small faux product catalog as a data package and show it on a new page in the GoReactChat web app.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: PGDataLayer defines JSON Schemas for category and product, with ~25 faux products across 5 categories as JSON files.
AC2: PGDataLayer CI validates every data file against its schema and fails on a product whose categoryId does not exist.
AC3: PGDataLayer ships committed TypeScript types generated from the schemas, and CI fails if they are out of date.
AC4: GoReactChat web has a /catalog page listing products grouped by category, using the typed data from the pgdatalayer package.
AC5: GoReactChat web builds and its tests pass against the PGDataLayer commit from the same change.
guidance: Data is consumed at build time as an npm package installed from GitHub at a full commit SHA. No API, no Postgres.
PGDataLayer must not have a prepare/build script; commit generated files.
Reuse the existing Tailwind styling in web/. Do not touch the Go server or the chat page.

plan.summary: PGDataLayer gets two JSON Schemas (category, product) and two data files (5 categories, about 25 products). Its existing `npm test` / `npm run check` hooks will validate the data, catch any product whose categoryId points to a missing category, and fail if the committed TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`, generated from the schemas) are stale. GoReactChat's web/ installs pgdatalayer from GitHub at the full commit SHA of the PGDataLayer change and adds a statically rendered /catalog page that groups products by category, styled with the existing Tailwind classes. A vitest unit test is added so `npm test` runs in web-ci.
approach: Data, schemas: add `schema/category.schema.json` (draft 2020-12; id as a slug pattern, name, optional description; additionalProperties false) and `schema/product.schema.json` (id, name, categoryId, priceCents as an integer ≥ 0, currency fixed to "USD", description, inStock boolean; additionalProperties false). Each file gets a `title` (Category / Product) so the generated type names are stable. Each data file is an array, so the validator checks each item against its entity schema.

Data, data files: `data/categories.json` holds 5 categories and `data/products.json` about 25 faux products (5 per category). The names match the README example `pgdatalayer/data/products.json`. Remove `data/.gitkeep` and `schema/.gitkeep`.

Data, validator: `scripts/validate.mjs` exports `validateCatalog({categories, products})`. It uses Ajv 2020 + ajv-formats (devDependencies) to check each item against its schema, then checks unique ids and that every product.categoryId exists in categories. It returns a list of errors. A `scripts/datasets.mjs` map (data file → schema) keeps 'every data file' explicit, and the test fails if a JSON file in data/ has no mapping.

Data, types: `scripts/gen-types.mjs` uses json-schema-to-typescript (devDependency) to compile both schemas into one `index.d.ts`, exporting `Category` and `Product` with a fixed banner and no timestamp so output is deterministic. `npm run gen:types` writes the file. `npm run check` runs `scripts/check-types.mjs`, which builds the same output in memory, compares it byte-for-byte with the committed `index.d.ts`, and exits 1 with a 'run npm run gen:types' message if they differ.

Data, package.json: add `"types": "./index.d.ts"` and an exports entry `".": { "types": "./index.d.ts" }`, keep the existing `./data/*` and `./schema/*` exports, add a `files` list covering data, schema and index.d.ts, add scripts `check` and `gen:types`, and add devDependencies (ajv, ajv-formats, json-schema-to-typescript) with an updated package-lock.json. No prepare/postinstall/build script, per sponsor guidance. Update README with the new scripts.

Data, tests (run by the existing `npm test` = `node --test`): `test/catalog.test.mjs` validates the real data files (AC1 counts: exactly 5 categories, 20–30 products, every category used). It also runs `validateCatalog` against fixtures in `test/fixtures/`: one with a dangling categoryId and one with a schema violation. Both must return errors, which proves CI fails on them. `test/types.test.mjs` checks that `index.d.ts` is current, so staleness also fails `npm test`.

Web, dependency: add `"pgdatalayer": "github:notbobutah/PGDataLayer#<40-char SHA of the data change>"` to web/package.json dependencies and regenerate web/package-lock.json. Assumption: the pipeline gives us the data commit SHA after the data component is committed, and web is pinned to that exact SHA (AC5). Never use a branch name.

Web, lib: `src/lib/catalog.ts` imports `categories` and `products` from `pgdatalayer/data/*.json` (resolveJsonModule is already on), imports the `Category` and `Product` types from `pgdatalayer`, and exposes typed arrays. It also exports a pure `groupProductsByCategory(categories, products)` that returns `[{ category, products }]` in category order with products sorted by name, plus `formatPrice(cents)`.

Web, page: add `src/app/catalog/page.tsx` as a server component (no 'use client'; prerendered statically at build time; no fetch, no API). It exports `metadata` (title 'Catalog'), renders an `<h1>` plus one `<section>` per category containing a list of product cards with name, description, price and an out-of-stock badge. It reuses the utility-class vocabulary already in news-panel.tsx/globals.css (text-black/70, dark:text-white/70, rounded, bg-black/[0.06], and so on). The Go server, chat.tsx, page.tsx and layout.tsx are left alone.

Web, tests: add vitest as a devDependency and a `"test": "vitest run"` script, so web-ci's `npm test --if-present` runs. Add `vitest.config.mts` with the `@/` alias and node environment. `src/lib/catalog.test.ts` tests grouping (every product appears once, under the right category, in category order) against fixtures and against the real pgdatalayer data. Before writing the page, read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` as AGENTS.md requires (Next 16.3 conventions).

outOfScope: Any API, Postgres, or runtime data fetching
Changes to the Go server, the chat page (page.tsx, chat.tsx), layout.tsx, or navigation links to /catalog
Changes to .github workflows, .agentic config, Dockerfile, or deploy manifests
Product images, search/filter, cart, or product detail pages
Publishing pgdatalayer to an npm registry
risks: Pinning the SHA: the web lockfile must reference the exact data commit. If the data commit is amended or rebased after web is pinned, web CI installs stale or missing data.

Installing from GitHub without git: node:24-alpine (Dockerfile) and CI rely on npm fetching the hosted-git tarball from codeload. This works only while pgdatalayer has no prepare script and the repo stays public, or CI has a token.
Type generation drift: different json-schema-to-typescript versions or formatting can change the output. Pin the exact devDependency version and use a fixed banner so check-types stays deterministic.
Next 16.3 may differ from familiar conventions (AGENTS.md warns), e.g. typed routes and LayoutProps. Running `next typegen` in typecheck must accept the new route.
Adding vitest to web increases install size and could clash with ESLint or tsconfig include globs. The config file is kept minimal.

body.text: Using Write instead.
Catalog file fails as a whole; let me see why (likely the Ajv import).
Dev dependencies were being skipped by the environment's npm config; installed with `--include=dev`. Re-running tests now.

I wrote the planned PGDataLayer tests. All 27 fail right now, which is expected because the implementation doesn't exist yet. Every failure comes from a missing schema, data file, script, `index.d.ts` or `package.json` field, and none from a syntax or setup error.

**What the tests cover:**
- **AC1 (schemas and data):** both schemas use draft 2020-12, carry the titles Category and Product, reject
Now writing the schemas and data.
I'll create the files with the Write tool.
Now package.json.
Types look good. Now remove the `.gitkeep` placeholders and run the verification commands.
I'll run the commands one at a time.
`npm ci` removed node_modules entirely because npm's `omit` is set to `dev` here. I'll find out where that setting comes from.
I'm not allowed to read the environment directly, so I'll stop probing it and run the tests to see what happens.
As expected: npm is set to omit devDependencies here, so `npm ci` doesn't install ajv or json-schema-to-typescript. To check my own code I'll install with `--include=dev`.
All passing. The lockfile already locked these devDependencies, so it didn't need to change. Last step is the README.
node_modules looks incomplete, so I'm doing a clean install from the lockfile.
That failure is expected because `catalog.ts` doesn't exist yet. To confirm the `@/` alias resolves, I'll add a temporary stub, run the tests, then delete it.
Bash isn't available in this session, so I'll look around the repo with the file tools.
package.json and the vitest config are already in place. Next I'll check the lockfile and node_modules.
Now I'll write the lib and the page.
The code is written. I'll try running the verification commands once more.
Bash works now. The commands have to run from the repository directory (`/work/repos/web`), so that `cd web` lands in the project root.
Only the exact verification commands seem to be allowed. I'll try a plain `cd` into the repository directory so those commands resolve correctly.
Lint and typecheck pass. Running tests and the build next.
